How Much House Can I Afford in Southern California?

A Real Buyer's Guide to Knowing Your Number Before You Start Looking

By Rudy Corona · February 11, 2026

The Question Every Buyer Starts With

It is the first thing that pops into your head the moment buying a home starts feeling real. Before you look at listings. Before you call a real estate agent. Before anything else, you want to know one thing: can I actually afford this?

It is a good question. And I want to give you a straight answer, because I work with first-time buyers across Southern California every week, and I see how much confusion exists around this topic. The good news is that affordability is not a mystery. It is math. And once you understand the math, you can approach the process with real confidence instead of guessing.

How Lenders Calculate What You Can Borrow

When a lender evaluates how much home you can afford, they are looking at two numbers above everything else: your income and your existing debt. They combine these into something called your debt-to-income ratio, or DTI.

Your DTI is calculated as your total monthly debt payments divided by your gross monthly income. Lenders look at two versions: Front-end DTI (just your future housing payment divided by gross income; most want this at or below 28% to 31%) and Back-end DTI (all monthly debt including housing; conventional typically wants 43% to 45%; FHA can go up to 57% with compensating factors).

Example: You earn $7,500 per month before taxes. You have a $400 car payment and $200 in minimum credit card payments ($600/month existing debt). At 43% back-end DTI, the lender would allow up to $3,225/month total debt. So your maximum housing payment would be $3,225 minus $600, or $2,625/month. That is your ceiling.

What Your Monthly Budget Buys You in Southern California

Southern California has some of the highest home prices in the country. Here is a realistic look at what different monthly payment budgets translate to (approximate 2024–25 rate ranges):

Monthly Budget (PITI)Approx. Loan AmountPrice Range (10% Down)Price Range (20% Down)
$2,000/month~$300,000$333,000$375,000
$2,500/month~$380,000$422,000$475,000
$3,000/month~$455,000$505,000$570,000
$3,500/month~$530,000$588,000$663,000
$4,000/month~$605,000$672,000$757,000
$5,000/month~$755,000$839,000$945,000

These numbers use rough estimates and will vary based on your exact rate, property taxes, insurance, and HOA. In many SoCal counties, property taxes alone can add $500–$800 per month to your payment on a $600,000 home. Build that into your calculation from the start.

The Income You Need to Qualify in SoCal

Working backwards, here is a general guide to household income typically needed at common SoCal price points:

Home PriceDown (10%)Loan AmountEst. Monthly PITIIncome Needed (Approx.)
$500,000$50,000$450,000~$3,300~$85,000/year
$650,000$65,000$585,000~$4,200~$110,000/year
$800,000$80,000$720,000~$5,100~$135,000/year
$1,000,000$100,000$900,000~$6,200~$165,000/year

These are household income estimates — a couple buying together can combine qualifying income. Two incomes can open doors that one income cannot.

Three Things That Can Change Your Number

1. Your credit score — It determines your interest rate, which significantly changes your monthly payment. Improving your credit before you buy can increase your purchasing power without increasing your income.

2. Your existing debt — Every monthly debt obligation reduces the housing payment a lender will allow. Paying down a car loan or eliminating a credit card balance before you apply can meaningfully increase how much home you qualify for.

3. Your down payment amount — A larger down payment means a smaller loan, a lower monthly payment, and a higher-priced home within the same monthly budget. It also eliminates or reduces PMI.

The Real First Step: Get Pre-Approved

A pre-approval is not just paperwork. It is the document that tells you your real number, not a guess from an online calculator. It also tells sellers that you are a serious buyer — which matters in a competitive Southern California market. The process takes a few days, requires basic documentation, and costs you nothing.
